<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="BRPXQZME" />{{running header|{{smaller|{{asc|ODE 3.}}}}|{{asc|THE MAJOR ODES OF THE KINGDOM.}}|383}}{{rule}}</noinclude><ref follow="p416_r3">remains in the small department of [[w:Binzhou, Shaanxi|Pin ''K''âu]], in [[w:Shaanxi|Shen-hsî]]. The [[wikt:沮|''Kh''ü]] flows into the [[w:Luo River|Lo]], and the [[wikt:漆|''Kh''î]] into the [[w:Wei River|Wei]].</ref>{{tooltip|Than-fû|Dǎnfù}}{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Made for them kiln-like huts and caves,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Ere they had yet any houses<ref>According to this ode then, up to the time of [[w:King Tai of Zhou|Than-fû]], the ''K''âu people had only had the dwellings here described; but this is not easily reconciled with other accounts, or even with other stanzas of this piece.</ref>.

The ancient duke Than-fû{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Came in the morning, galloping his horses,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Along the banks of the western rivers,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
To the foot of mount {{tooltip|''Kh''î|Qí}}<ref>See a graphic account of the circumstances in which this migration took place, in the fifteenth chapter of the second Part of the first Book of [[Mencius]], very much to the honour of the ancient duke.</ref>;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And there he and the lady {{tooltip|''K''iang|Jiāng}}<ref>This lady is known as [[w:zh:太姜|Thâi-''k''iang]], the worthy predecessor of [[w:Tai Ren|Thâi-''z''ăn]].</ref>{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Came and together looked out for a site.

{{anchor|st3}}The plain of {{tooltip|''K''âu|Zhōu}} looked beautiful and rich,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
With its violets, and sowthistles (sweet) as dumplings.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
There he began by consulting (with his followers);{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
There he singed the tortoise-shell, (and divined).{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The responses were there to stay and then;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And they proceeded there to build<ref>This stanza has reference to the choice—by council and divination—of a site for what should be the chief town of the new settlement.</ref>.

He encouraged the people, and settled them;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Here on the left, there on the right.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He divided the ground, and subdivided it;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He dug the ditches; he defined the acres.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
From the east to the west,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
There was nothing which he did not take in hand<ref>This stanza describes the general arrangements for the occupancy and cultivation of [[w:Guanzhong|the plain]] of [[w:Predynastic Zhou|''K''âu]], and the distribution of the people over it.</ref>.
